source.title: Some Lessons Learned from Studying Indirect Object Identification in GPT-2 small

record.file_problem: None; the full post and its comments are present.
record.tranche_reason: The post reports the original circuit’s knockout and patching evaluations, and a comment reports additional causal-scrubbing tests of the circuit.
record.gate_note: The post reports circuit evaluations, patching effects, a prompt-distribution result, and an adversarial prompt result. The causal-scrubbing results and the mean-absolute-logit-difference criticism appear in comments. It also discusses earlier mean-ablation results that were misleading because the replacement activations retained task-relevant information. Historical claims and results cited from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The post is the original authors' companion to arXiv:2211.00593, and its own results are the original paper's. The new evidence is co-author Alexandre Variengien's causal-scrubbing comment, a different, path-based method applied to the same circuit hypothesis. Only those rows (r6, r7) get verdicts.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The post's authors say their three criteria partially validate the circuit but leave gaps, and that per-template circuits probably differ subtly. The causal-scrubbing commenter is himself a paper co-author. He judges the circuit one of the best small sets of paths, though many undescribed paths matter. This lowered his confidence without strongly questioning the paper's claims.
record.recipe_differences: Companion post to the original study, describing its mean-ablation and activation/path-patching approach; a comment adds causal scrubbing, a stricter path-based test.
record.method_sensitivity: Results differ with the mean-ablation replacement distribution, with causal scrubbing versus mean ablation, and with the evaluation metric. Logit differences also vary across templates.
record.peer_reviewed: ICLR 2023 (the paper, as stated in a comment); this record is an Alignment Forum post.
record.problems: The causal-scrubbing results are noisy, with reported uncertainties large relative to the means; the commenter reports N=100 and says the noise source is not understood. The post notes substantial template-to-template logit-difference variation and does not explain it. Several circuit findings are stated qualitatively without detailed conditions or numerical measurements.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant reported results were left out.

untested.parts: No new test. There is only a restatement of the original's backup-head finding.
Other models, sizes, checkpoints and task reuse are named only as future work.
No new test across name orders, templates or more names. The adversarial and template-variance points are the original's results, or speculation.

record.verdict_notes: The post is a companion piece by the original authors, so its main-text results (r1–r5, r8) are original-source results and get no verdicts. The causal-scrubbing comment is new work by an original co-author; it gets verdicts but is not independent. The scrubbing numbers have standard deviations larger than their means (N=100). LawrenceC's metric criticism gives no number.

versions.untested_parts: The post does not provide a complete numerical evaluation of every head class, or detailed results for all faithfulness, completeness, and minimality tests.
The post does not give a quantitative measure or detailed patching evidence for backup-head compensation.
Other models, sizes, checkpoints, and reuse of the components for other tasks are described as future work, not tested here.
The post does not systematically compare a range of circuit-finding methods; it reports sensitivity to ablation choices and a comment’s criticism of an alternative metric.
The post does not provide a systematic sweep over ablation types, metrics, and prompt distributions.
It does not test a systematic range of templates or prompts with more than two names, nor establish that the same components carry the behavior across them.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.operation_detail: Ablating heads and identifying other heads that compensate for lost function.
rows.value: The authors report finding heads that compensate for the loss of function of other heads.
rows.note: The post does not specify the ablated heads, the compensating heads, or the size of the effect.
rows.check: Restates the original paper's backup-head finding qualitatively, with no heads or numbers. It is an original-source result, so no verdict.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.operation_detail: Mean-ablating nodes outside the proposed circuit to evaluate faithfulness.
rows.measure: Logit difference retained by the circuit
rows.note: The post does not specify the ablation distribution for this reported score.
rows.check: The 87% faithfulness score is cited from the original paper, and the comment uses it as a comparator. It should be role comparator. 87% is close to full, not partial.

source_check.correct: Retain 87% as a cited comparator from the original paper; change role from main to comparator.

source_check.problem: The numerical fields are correct, but this is a cited result rather than a new main result.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.operation_detail: Mean-ablating induction heads and duplicate-token heads using means from an IOI-distribution template.
rows.value: The ablations had little effect; the means retained the fact that a name was duplicated.
rows.locator: Knockouts and Patching are Tricky: Do You Have the Right Distribution?
rows.note: The post says this earlier ablation choice was a poor test because task-relevant information remained in the replacement activations.
rows.check: An anecdote from earlier versions of the original work. It shows that the choice of mean-ablation distribution hid the importance of the induction and duplicate-token heads, which is evidence on ablation sensitivity (V5), not on the final circuit (V1). It is an original-source result.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.operation_detail: Patching head outputs between ABBA and BABA prompts, in both directions.
rows.note: The post interprets this as evidence that S-Inhibition Heads provide positional clues used by Name Movers.
rows.check: The original paper's Appendix A probe of S-Inhibition positional signals. It does not test whether the circuit carries IOI across name orders, so V6 is removed. It is an original-source result.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.operation_detail: Adding a distractor sentence that repeats the indirect-object name.

conditions.value: IO name repeated in a distractor sentence

rows.measure: Frequency of predicting S over IO
rows.locator: Adversarial Examples: Using your understanding to generate predictions
rows.note: This shows a failure on the modified prompt format; it does not independently identify which components produce the failure.
rows.check: The original paper's adversarial result (23.4% vs 0.7%). It confirms a failure the circuit predicts, but does not show which components act on the modified format. It is an original-source result.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.operation_detail: Causal scrubbing, allowing all MLP paths while leaving only circuit attention heads unscrubbed, split by keys, queries, values, and position.

conditions.value: Only circuit heads non-scrubbed, split by key, query, value, and position

rows.measure: Scrubbed-model logit difference and percentage of original
rows.baseline: Original logit difference; absolute baseline not stated
rows.note: The commenter says resampling ablation is more destructive than mean ablation here and that causal scrubbing selects paths rather than nodes.
rows.check: Causal scrubbing of the circuit with all MLPs allowed recovers 50%±57 of the logit difference, against 87% faithfulness under mean ablation. The study's own noise is very large.

source_check.locator_found: Alexandre Variengien comment, Experiment 1, lines 218 and 222; sample size at line 246.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.operation_detail: Causal scrubbing with selected paths allowed to queries, keys, values, and MLPs at specified positions; only direct head-to-head interactions inside the circuit preserved.

conditions.value: Paths to Name Movers' keys and values at IO and S1; to S-Inhibition queries at END; to Duplicate Token and Induction queries at S2; to Duplicate Token keys and values at S1 and IO; and to Previous Token values at S1 and IO

rows.measure: Scrubbed-model logit difference and percentage of original
rows.baseline: Original logit difference; absolute baseline not stated
rows.note: The commenter interprets this as evidence that more paths matter than the proposed circuit captures.
rows.check: The stricter path-based scrubbing recovers 22%±64 of the logit difference. The uncertainty is very large.

source_check.locator_found: Alexandre Variengien comment, Experiment 2, lines 226–240; sample size at line 246.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.operation_detail: Measuring logit-difference variability across the prompt distribution.

conditions.value: Different templates in the studied distribution

rows.uncertainty: The value is the reported standard deviation, approximately 40% of the logit difference.
rows.locator: How We Chose This Problem: Picking the Task is Important; Alexandre Variengien comment
rows.note: The post says the authors did not have good hypotheses for the variation and suspected circuits for individual templates could differ subtly; it does not measure circuit fidelity separately by template.
rows.check: This is variability of the model's own logit difference. The claim that per-template circuits differ is the authors' speculation and was not measured. The value is an original-source result. V5 is removed.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.operation_detail: Replacing mean logit difference with mean absolute logit difference as the circuit-evaluation metric.
rows.measure: Whether the proposed circuit holds up under the alternative metric
rows.value: A reviewer/commenter states that the circuit does not hold up well under the alternative metric.
rows.note: The comment gives no numerical result for the alternative metric.
rows.check: A reviewer's assertion with no reported number, partly based on reviews elsewhere. It bears on metric sensitivity, but the value cannot be read. V4 is removed: no alternative method is compared.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.operation_detail: Measuring original-model logit-difference variability on the causal-scrubbing dataset.
rows.measure: Standard deviation relative to mean logit difference
rows.value: Standard deviation around 30% of the mean
rows.uncertainty: The reported standard deviation is around 30% of the mean.
rows.note: This describes variation in the original model's measurement, not a direct comparison of circuit fidelity across prompts.
rows.check: This is variability of the original model's logit difference. It measures no circuit property and no prompt-variant property.

relationships.reason: Under scrubbing the circuit recovers only 50% (r6) or 22% (r7) of the logit difference, not the 87% reported for faithfulness.
